rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
The rule on when Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) starts is in MuSchG §3(1). Your employer may not employ you "in den letzten sechs Wochen vor der Entbindung" (in the last six weeks before the birth). The law calls this the "Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung" (protection period before the birth).

How the six weeks are measured: they count back from the expected date of birth shown on the certificate from your doctor, midwife or Entbindungspfleger ("der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung … wie er sich aus dem ärztlichen Zeugnis oder dem Zeugnis einer Hebamme oder eines Entbindungspflegers ergibt"). Six weeks before an expected date of 15 November 2026 falls in early October 2026. The excerpts do not say how the exact first day is counted.

Conditions the law attaches:
- You may still work during these six weeks if you expressly declare that you are willing to ("soweit sie sich nicht zur Arbeitsleistung ausdrücklich bereit erklärt"). You can withdraw that declaration at any time, with effect for the future.
- If the baby is not born on the expected date, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match.

After the birth, your employer may not employ you until eight weeks have passed. This extends to twelve weeks:
1. for premature births,
2. for multiple births, and
3. if, within eight weeks of the birth, a doctor finds that the child has a disability within the meaning of § 2(1) sentence 1 SGB IX. This extension applies only if you apply for it.

If the baby comes early, the period after the birth is also extended by the time the period before the birth was shortened.

The Mutterschutz law (Mutterschutzgesetz) does not cover self-employed women. They need to arrange their own cover for the time before and after the birth.

Whether and how these rules apply to your own job is not decided here. Your employer applies the protection period. For Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay), your Krankenkasse (health insurance fund) is the body to contact.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
There is no fixed application deadline in the law, but late applications lose money. Elterngeld (parental allowance) must be applied for in writing. It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month of life in which the application is received. Months before that are not paid.

Counted this way, an application received during the child's fourth month of life still reaches back to the first month. An application received later loses the earliest months, one for each month of delay.

Elterngeld can be drawn from the day of birth, and is paid in monthly amounts for the child's months of life, not calendar months. Basic Elterngeld can be drawn until the child completes its 14th month of life. These limits differ for children born early.

What you receive, and for which months, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle responsible for your district.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
The notice period for Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) depends on when the leave falls in your child's life. Under BEEG §16(1), you must request it from your employer in text form at least:

- seven weeks before the leave starts, for leave in the period up to your child's third birthday ("spätestens sieben Wochen");
- 13 weeks before the leave starts, for leave between the third birthday and the end of the child's eighth year ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

The request must be made "in Textform". The Familienportal explains that this can be, for example, a letter without a signature or an email.

When you request leave for the period up to the third birthday, you must also state at the same time which periods within two years you will take as Elternzeit. If the mother takes Elternzeit straight after her maternity protection period, that period counts towards the two years. If she first takes holiday after maternity protection, both the maternity protection period and the holiday count towards the two years.

The law allows exceptions. Where there are urgent reasons, a reasonable shorter period is possible as an exception ("Bei dringenden Gründen ist ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist möglich"). The law does not set what counts as urgent. If a mother cannot request Elternzeit in time to follow directly on her maternity protection period, for a reason that is not her fault, she can make the request within one week after that reason ends (BEEG §16(2)).

Your employer must confirm your Elternzeit to you in writing ("Der Arbeitgeber hat ... die Elternzeit zu bescheinigen").

The Familienportal page describes a different notice rule for children born before 1 July 2015. The statutory transitional provision behind that is not among the sources I have, so I cannot confirm which rule applies to an earlier birth.

Elternzeit is requested from your employer, not from a public office.

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
After the birth, Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) normally lasts eight weeks. During this time the employer may not employ the mother ("bis zum Ablauf von acht Wochen nach der Entbindung nicht beschäftigen", MuSchG §3(2)).

If the baby comes before the expected date, the law adds the lost days. The six-week period before the birth is counted from the expected date of delivery. If the birth is earlier, that period is shortened (MuSchG §3(1)). The period after the birth is then extended by exactly the time the period before the birth was shortened ("verlängert sich die Schutzfrist nach der Entbindung ... um den Zeitraum der Verkürzung der Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung", MuSchG §3(2)). The official family portal says the same: the total period stays at 14 weeks.

The period after the birth is extended to twelve weeks in three cases (MuSchG §3(2)):
1. a premature birth ("Frühgeburten");
2. a multiple birth, such as twins or triplets;
3. a doctor finds a disability in the child, within the meaning of § 2(1) sentence 1 of SGB IX, before the eight weeks after the birth have ended. In this case the extension applies only if the mother applies for it.

If an early birth also counts as a premature birth, both rules apply together. The twelve weeks are extended further by the time the period before the birth was shortened (MuSchG §3(2)). The statute does not define a premature birth. The official family portal gives a birth weight under 2,500 grams as one example of a birth that counts medically as premature. It says the total period then rises from 14 to 18 weeks.

The twelve-week extension in point 1 to 3 does not apply to a stillbirth (MuSchG §3(2)).

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
Generally no. During pregnancy, your employer may dismiss you only in rare exceptional cases, and only with official approval.

What the law says. Under the Mutterschutzgesetz, dismissal of a woman is "unzulässig" (not permitted) in three periods:
1. during her pregnancy,
2. until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy, and
3. until the end of her protection period after the birth, and at least until four months after the birth.

When the protection applies. It applies if your employer knows about the pregnancy, miscarriage or birth when dismissing you, or if you tell them within two weeks of receiving the dismissal ("innerhalb von zwei Wochen nach Zugang der Kündigung"). Missing those two weeks does no harm if the delay was not your fault and you tell them "unverzüglich" (without delay). The Familienportal adds that the Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) applies even if you did not yet know you were pregnant. However, you must already have been pregnant when the dismissal was given.

The exception. In special cases not connected with your pregnancy, a miscarriage or the birth, "die für den Arbeitsschutz zuständige oberste Landesbehörde oder die von ihr bestimmte Stelle" can exceptionally declare a dismissal permitted. This is the highest state authority for occupational safety, or a body it designates. The dismissal must then be in writing and must state the reason. The Familienportal gives these as examples of such special reasons:
- insolvency of the company,
- partial closure of the business,
- in a small business, that it cannot continue without a qualified replacement,
- a particularly serious breach of duty.
The employer must apply in writing to the supervisory authority. Without its approval, the dismissal is "unwirksam" (invalid).

If you are dismissed without approval. According to the Familienportal, you must bring a claim before the competent labour court ("Klage vor dem zuständigen Arbeitsgericht"). It says the claim must "normalerweise innerhalb von 3 Wochen" be filed from receipt of the written dismissal. If you do not bring a claim, the dismissal counts as legally effective ("gilt die Kündigung Ihres Arbeitgebers als rechtswirksam"). The page also says you should involve the competent supervisory authority.

If you take Elternzeit after the birth, separate protection against dismissal under BEEG §18 can follow on.

Whether any of this applies to your own situation, and whether a particular dismissal is valid, is not something this service can decide. The supervisory authority for maternity protection in your state, and the labour court, are the bodies responsible.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under BEEG §1(8), the entitlement to Elterngeld (parental allowance) lapses ("Ein Anspruch entfällt") if the entitled person had zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income) of more than 175,000 euros ("in Höhe von mehr als 175 000 Euro") in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth ("im letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum vor der Geburt des Kindes").

Where another person also meets the conditions, for example the other parent living in the same household with the child, the limit applies to the combined figure: the entitlement lapses if "die Summe des zu versteuernden Einkommens beider Personen mehr als 175 000 Euro beträgt" (the taxable income of both persons together exceeds 175,000 euros).

The limit refers to taxable income as defined in § 2 Absatz 5 of the Einkommensteuergesetz, not gross income. The official Familienportal explains that taxable income is usually considerably lower than gross income, because items such as special expenses, provision expenses, individual allowances and extraordinary burdens are deducted. It also says the individual figure is determined by the Finanzamt and appears in the tax assessment notice.

If the tax assessment notice for the last completed assessment period is not yet available when applying, BEEG §8 provides for this. If it cannot yet be stated whether the limit is exceeded, the amount is decided provisionally ("vorläufig"). If the application states the limit will probably not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation ("unter dem Vorbehalt des Widerrufs") in case it turns out to be exceeded.

The 175,000 euro figure is the one the statute states. The Familienportal says different limits applied to births before 1 April 2025. The statutory transitional rules for earlier births are not in the excerpts available here, so this answer does not say which limit applies to a particular birth. That, and whether the limit affects your own entitlement, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle (parental allowance office) responsible for your district.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
The law sets the number of months; it does not decide what your family receives. Elterngeld (parental allowance) is paid in monthly amounts for the child's months of life, counted from the date of birth, not calendar months (BEEG §4(2)).

Basic form: parents together are entitled to 12 monthly amounts ("zwölf Monatsbeträge Basiselterngeld"). They get 2 further months, called partner months, if one parent's earned income is reduced in two months of the child's life ("zwei weitere Monate Basiselterngeld (Partnermonate)"). That makes 14 basic months for the couple (BEEG §4(3)).

Plus form: instead of one basic month, a parent can take two months of the Plus form ("jeweils zwei Lebensmonate Elterngeld Plus") (BEEG §4(3)).

Per parent: one parent can receive at most 12 basic monthly amounts plus at most 4 monthly amounts of partnership bonus under §4b. A parent only has a claim if they receive Elterngeld for at least 2 months of the child's life (BEEG §4(4)). The official family portal describes the partnership bonus as up to 4 extra months of the Plus form for each parent when both work part-time at the same time (familienportal.de). The excerpts do not contain the text of §4b itself.

Time limits: the basic form can be received until the child completes the 14th month of life. The Plus form can be received until the child completes the 32nd month of life, as long as at least one parent takes it in consecutive months from the 15th month (BEEG §4(1)).

Premature births: the joint basic entitlement is higher if the child was born early, measured from the expected delivery date in the doctor's or midwife's certificate (BEEG §4(5)):
- at least 6 weeks early: 13 monthly amounts
- at least 8 weeks early: 14 monthly amounts
- at least 12 weeks early: 15 monthly amounts
- at least 16 weeks early: 16 monthly amounts
In these cases the per-parent maximum rises to the same number (13 to 16), plus up to 4 months of partnership bonus. The basic form can then be received until the 15th, 16th, 17th or 18th month of life respectively (BEEG §4(5)).

How many months your family actually receives is decided by the Elterngeldstelle (parental allowance office) for your district.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) gives each parent extra months of payment when both parents work part-time at the same time.

What it is: under BEEG §4b(1), if both parents work "nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats" (no fewer than 24 and no more than 32 hours a week, averaged over the month of the child's life), and both meet the conditions of BEEG §1, each parent is entitled to "einen zusätzlichen Monatsbetrag Elterngeld Plus" (an additional monthly amount of Elterngeld Plus) for that month. The excerpts do not set out the conditions of §1 themselves.

The rules that apply to couples:
- Each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts of the Partnerschaftsbonus, and only if each takes it for at least two months of the child's life (BEEG §4b(2)). BEEG §4(4) confirms these up to four months come on top of the basic entitlement.
- Both parents must take it at the same time, in consecutive months of the child's life (BEEG §4b(3)).
- The consecutive-months requirement still counts as met if it later turns out that the conditions were not met in every month applied for (BEEG §4b(5)).

One parent alone: BEEG §4c(2) gives one parent additional monthly amounts of Elterngeld Plus if that parent works 24 to 32 hours a week on average in at least two and at most four consecutive months, and one of these three grounds in BEEG §4c(1) applies:
1. the parent meets the conditions for the tax relief for single parents under §24b(1) and (3) of the Income Tax Act, and the other parent lives neither with them nor with the child;
2. care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare within the meaning of §1666(1) and (2) of the Civil Code; or
3. care by the other parent is impossible, in particular because of serious illness or severe disability; economic reasons and being occupied with other activities do not count.
If one of these grounds arises while both parents are already receiving the bonus, one parent can continue it under §4c(2) (BEEG §4b(4)).

Amount: the federal guidance page says the bonus is calculated the same way as Elterngeld Plus and, depending on income before the birth, is between 150 and 900 euros a month per parent. It also says that if your hours in a month fall outside 24 to 32, the bonus for that month must be repaid, and you must report the change.

The guidance notes that its explanations cover children born after August 2021, and that partly different rules apply to children born before 1 September 2021.

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive, is decided only by the parental allowance office responsible for your district.

rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid backdated for at most six months. The law says payment is made retroactively "nur für die letzten sechs Monate vor Beginn des Monats, in dem der Antrag auf Kindergeld eingegangen ist": only for the last six months before the start of the month in which the application is received. The same provision says the underlying entitlement is not affected by this payment limit ("Der Anspruch auf Kindergeld nach § 62 bleibt von dieser Auszahlungsbeschränkung unberührt"). The limit is on how far back payment goes. It is not a cut-off for applying.

Kindergeld must be applied for in writing, at the responsible Familienkasse. The official family portal says to submit the application to the Familienkasse at your Agentur für Arbeit. For a backdated claim, it says to state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when you want to receive Kindergeld.

The Familienkasse decides whether you are entitled and for which months.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?
rows.reply:
The law sets one monthly amount per child, and it is the same for a first child as for any other. Kindergeld (child benefit) is 259 euros a month for each child. Both statutes state it in the same words: "Das Kindergeld beträgt monatlich für jedes Kind 259 Euro" (EStG §66(1); BKGG §6(1)).

Kindergeld is paid monthly, "vom Beginn des Monats an", from the start of the month in which the conditions for it are met. It runs until the end of the month in which those conditions stop being met (EStG §66(2)). Both statutes also provide that Kindergeld is raised if the tax allowances for children are raised (EStG §66(3); BKGG §6(2)).

This is the amount the law sets. Whether your family is entitled to it is decided by the responsible authority, not here. The federal family portal points to the online Kindergeld application at the Bundesagentur für Arbeit. It also says the Finanzamt automatically checks, in the annual income tax assessment, whether the tax allowances for children or the Kindergeld paid are more favourable for the parents.

rows.question: How quickly do we have to register the birth at the Standesamt?
rows.reply:
The birth must be reported to the Standesamt (civil registry office) for the area where the child was born "binnen einer Woche" (within one week) of the birth. The law allows this report to come either from the persons it names, orally or in writing, or from the institutions it names, in writing.

If the child was born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the official family portal says the institution notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends the birth certificate from the birth. If the child was born at home, the midwife or doctor issues that certificate, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

For a stillbirth the period is shorter: the report must be made "spätestens am dritten auf die Geburt folgenden Werktag" (at the latest on the third working day after the birth).

The excerpts do not say what happens if the one-week period is missed. The Standesamt for the place of birth is the authority responsible. Its website lists which further documents it needs.

rows.question: What do we need to bring to the Standesamt to register the birth?
rows.reply:
The documents are set out in PStV §33. When a birth is registered, the Standesamt (civil registry office) 'soll ... verlangen' (is to ask for) the following:

1. If the parents are married to each other: their marriage certificate or a certified extract from the marriage register. They also need their own birth certificates if the parents' birth registration details do not appear on the marriage certificate. The marriage certificate is required even if the marriage has since been dissolved.
2. If the parents are not married to each other: the mother's birth certificate. If paternity has already been acknowledged, also the acknowledgement declarations and the father's birth certificate, and any joint custody declarations.
3. An identity card, passport or other recognised passport substitute for the parents.
4. If the birth is reported in person (orally): a certificate of the birth issued by a doctor or midwife who was present at the birth.

The Standesamt may ask for further documents where needed to prove the details given.

The birth certificate from the birth itself: if your child was born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the facility notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends it the birth certificate. If your child was born at home, the midwife or doctor issues it, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within 1 week.

If both parents are foreign nationals: under PStV §34, when the birth is registered the Standesamt asks whether either parent holds an unlimited right of residence (or a residence permit under the EU-Swiss free movement agreement). It uses this information to check whether the child acquired German citizenship by birth. The Standesamt carries out that check. This answer does not say what the outcome would be for your family.

The official family portal says that the website of the Standesamt in the place where your child is born lists any further documents. The responsible office is the Standesamt for the child's place of birth.

rows.question: Does my Krankenkasse pay for a midwife?
rows.reply:
Yes, under the statutory health insurance law, a woman insured with a Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer) is entitled to help from a Hebamme (midwife). SGB V §24d says the insured woman has a right to medical care and to midwife help "während der Schwangerschaft, bei und nach der Entbindung" (during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth). This includes the examinations to confirm the pregnancy and prenatal check-ups ("zur Feststellung der Schwangerschaft und zur Schwangerenvorsorge").

For care after the birth, the entitlement to Hebamme help lasts "bis zum Ablauf von zwölf Wochen nach der Geburt" (until twelve weeks after the birth). Further services beyond that need a doctor's order ("bedürfen der ärztlichen Anordnung").

If the mother cannot care for the baby after the birth, the insured child has its own right to the midwife services that relate to the child.

The Familienportal puts it plainly: every woman with statutory health insurance has a right to support from a Hebamme. If you have private health insurance instead, that page says to check with your insurer beforehand which services it covers. Private insurance is outside what this product covers.

Whether a specific service is covered in your case is decided by your Krankenkasse.

rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
The Kinder-Richtlinie (children's screening guideline) sets fixed time windows for the check-ups. Each has a normal period and an outer limit ("Toleranzgrenze"). The guideline says the check-ups "können nur in den jeweils angegebenen Zeiträumen" be used, meaning only within these windows.

The first ones are:

- U1: immediately after birth ("Unmittelbar nach der Geburt"). It should take place within the first 30 minutes after the birth ("innerhalb der ersten 30 Minuten nach der Geburt"). If no doctor is present at the birth but a midwife is, the midwife should carry it out.
- U2: 3rd to 10th day of life ("3.-10. Lebenstag"). Outer limit: 3rd to 14th day.
- U3: 4th to 5th week of life ("4.-5. Lebenswoche"). Outer limit: 3rd to 8th week.
- U4: 3rd to 4th month of life ("3.-4. Lebensmonat"). Outer limit: 2nd to 4½th month.
- U5: 6th to 7th month of life. Outer limit: 5th to 8th month.
- U6: 10th to 12th month of life. Outer limit: 9th to 14th month.

There are ten check-ups in total in the first six years, ending with U9 at 60 to 64 months.

The same time windows apply to babies born prematurely ("Auch bei Frühgeborenen sind die Untersuchungszeiträume einzuhalten"). The premature birth is taken into account when the results are assessed.

Children are entitled to these screening check-ups until their 18th birthday.

The G-BA (Federal Joint Committee) issues this guideline. Its website says the version currently offered does not yet include a decision that came into force on 20 August 2026. Check the G-BA page for the current version.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the protection periods before and after the birth, and for the day of the birth itself (MuSchG §19, SGB V §24i). The family portal says these protection periods normally begin 6 weeks before the calculated due date and end 8 weeks after the birth.

Who pays depends on your health insurance:

- If you are a member of a statutory health insurer, you receive Mutterschaftsgeld under the rules of the Social Code, Book V (MuSchG §19(1)). For members who are employed when the protection period starts, it is based on average net daily pay over the last three settled calendar months before that period, and it is at most 13 euros per calendar day ("höchstens 13 Euro für den Kalendertag", SGB V §24i(2)). Pay above that is made up by the employer as a top-up (MuSchG §20(1)).
- If you are not a member of a statutory health insurer, Mutterschaftsgeld is paid by the federal government, at most 210 euros in total ("insgesamt höchstens 210 Euro"). It is paid "auf Antrag" (on application) by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung (MuSchG §19(2)).

For payment before the birth, the decisive document is a certificate from a doctor or midwife stating the expected date of delivery (SGB V §24i(3)).

The claim is suspended while you receive pay subject to contributions, earned income or holiday compensation. One-off payments do not count (SGB V §24i(4)).

Mutterschaftsgeld from the statutory health insurer, and the employer top-up, are offset against Elterngeld for the time from the day of the birth. The 210-euro payment under MuSchG §19(2) is not offset (BEEG §3(1)).

When to apply: the excerpts do not state a time by which, or a point from which, you apply. If you have statutory insurance, ask your health insurer. If you do not, the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung is the body that pays. Whether you qualify, and how much you receive, is decided by the responsible body, not by this summary.

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
No. Under federal law, marriage is the only route to automatic legal fatherhood. BGB §1592 says the father of a child is the man who:
1. is married to the mother at the time of the birth ("zum Zeitpunkt der Geburt mit der Mutter des Kindes verheiratet ist"),
2. has acknowledged paternity ("die Vaterschaft anerkannt hat"), or
3. has had his paternity established by a court ("gerichtlich festgestellt").

The official family portal says the same: if the parents are not married at the time of the birth, the father must make a Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity) to count legally as the father. It is voluntary and needs the mother's consent.

Under BGB §1594:
- The Vaterschaftsanerkennung can be made before the child is born.
- It is not effective while another man's paternity exists.
- It is invalid if made subject to a condition or a time limit.

The family portal adds that if the mother is married to another man at the time of the birth, her husband is the legal father. In that case no Vaterschaftsanerkennung is possible, apart from a narrow exception connected with divorce. The portal notes that this part of its information is being updated after a recent change in the law.

Where to make it: the father must make the declaration in person at a competent office, for example the youth welfare office, a registry office, a local court or a notary. The mother must also give her consent in person. The office records both. Depending on the federal state, it can cost a fee at a notary or court.

Acknowledging paternity does not on its own give the father parental custody. For that, both parents must also declare that they want joint custody, or a court must decide. Your local youth welfare office advises on questions of paternity and custody.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
When parents are not married to each other at the birth, the mother has parental custody from the birth. Under the statute, the parents have joint custody in any of three cases: 1. they both declare that they want to take on custody jointly. This is a Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody), "wenn sie erklären, dass sie die Sorge gemeinsam übernehmen wollen (Sorgeerklärungen)". 2. They marry each other ("wenn sie einander heiraten"). 3. The family court transfers custody to them jointly ("soweit ihnen das Familiengericht die elterliche Sorge gemeinsam überträgt"). Otherwise, the mother has custody ("Im Übrigen hat die Mutter die elterliche Sorge").

The federal family portal adds a step that comes first. The other parent must be legally recognised as the father, either by acknowledging the child with the mother's consent or by a court establishing paternity. Recognition of paternity alone does not give custody. A Sorgeerklärung from both parents, or a court decision, is still needed.

The court route works like this. On the application of one parent, the family court transfers custody, or part of it, to both parents jointly if this does not run counter to the child's welfare ("wenn die Übertragung dem Kindeswohl nicht widerspricht"). It is presumed not to run counter to the child's welfare if the other parent puts forward no reasons against it and none are otherwise apparent. The family portal says that in that case the family court decides in a simplified procedure, without hearing the youth welfare office and without hearing the parents in person.

A Sorgeerklärung and a final court decision transferring joint custody are each entered in a custody register. That register is kept by the responsible youth welfare office.

The excerpts do not say where or in what form a Sorgeerklärung is made. Parents who are not married to each other have a legal right to advice from the youth welfare office on making a Sorgeerklärung and on the court route to joint custody. Your local youth welfare office is the place to ask about the procedure. Whether a court transfers custody in a particular case is decided by the family court.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Frankfurt?
rows.reply:
You apply to the Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance) responsible for where your child lives. Under federal law, each state decides which authorities carry out Elterngeld (parental allowance). The competent one is the authority of the district where the child has its residence in Germany when the first application is made: "Behörde des Bezirks, in dem das Kind … zum Zeitpunkt der ersten Antragstellung seinen inländischen Wohnsitz hat" (BEEG §12). For a child living in Frankfurt, that means the Elterngeldstelle that covers Frankfurt.

In Hessen, the Regierungspräsidium Gießen publishes the contact details of the six Hessian offices that handle Elterngeld ("sechs Hessischen Ämter für Versorgung und Soziales"). The excerpts do not say which of the six covers Frankfurt. Look it up on that contact page: https://rp-giessen.hessen.de/Elterngeld

You can apply in person at the Elterngeldstelle or digitally. A digital application is possible in every federal state. The application must be made in writing: "Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen" (BEEG §7). In the application, you state which months of life you are claiming Basiselterngeld, Elterngeld Plus or Partnerschaftsbonus for.

Timing matters. Elterngeld is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid (BEEG §7).

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Berlin?
rows.reply:
You apply to the Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance) responsible for your area. Federal law leaves it to each state to designate the office. The competent one is the office "des Bezirks, in dem das Kind ... zum Zeitpunkt der ersten Antragstellung seinen inländischen Wohnsitz hat", meaning the district where your child lives when you first apply (BEEG §12). The excerpts do not name the individual Berlin offices. Look for the Elterngeldstelle for your district on Service Berlin.

How to apply in Berlin:

- Elterngeld (parental allowance) must be applied for in writing: "Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen" (BEEG §7).
- Berlin is one of the states covered by ElterngeldDigital. A digital assistant helps you fill in the application. You then print the document, sign it and send it by post to your responsible Elterngeldstelle (Familienportal, ElterngeldDigital).
- Service Berlin also describes an online application. For this you sign in with a BundID account, or register for one if you do not have one (Service Berlin).
- If something changes after you have applied, such as the payment period or your bank details, Service Berlin directs you to the Berlin change application, the "Berliner Änderungsantrag auf Elterngeld".

Timing matters for payment. Elterngeld is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received: "rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats ..., in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist" (BEEG §7). Months before that are not paid.

Whether you are entitled, and to how much, is decided by your Elterngeldstelle.

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Not automatically because you are parents, but German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) can be acquired by birth in Germany if the law's conditions are met.

The law sets two routes by birth:

1. Through a parent. A child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth if a parent holds German Staatsangehörigkeit ("wenn ein Elternteil die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit besitzt", StAG §4(1)).

2. Through birth in Germany. A child of foreign parents born in Germany ("Durch die Geburt im Inland erwirbt ein Kind ausländischer Eltern die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit") acquires it if one parent meets both of these conditions (StAG §4(3)):
- has had their lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland"), and
- holds an unlimited right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"), or, as a Swiss citizen or family member of one, a residence permit under the 1999 EU–Switzerland free movement agreement.
The acquisition is entered in the birth register where the birth is recorded.

How this is checked. When the birth is registered, the registry office ("Standesamt") asks whether a parent holds an unlimited right of residence. If the information meets that condition, it obtains written information from the immigration authority ("Ausländerbehörde") on whether the information is correct and whether the parent had five years of lawful habitual residence in Germany at the time of the birth. The registry office then examines whether the child acquired German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth and records the result (PStV §34).

Whether your child meets these conditions is decided by the registry office that registers the birth, not by this service. Your local immigration authority holds the information on your own residence status.

If a child born in Germany does not become German, residence is covered by AufenthG §33. The child is granted a residence permit "von Amts wegen" (by the authority on its own initiative) if, at the birth, both parents (or the parent with sole custody) hold an Aufenthaltserlaubnis, a Niederlassungserlaubnis or an Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU. If only one parent holds one of these, a permit can be granted. If a parent holds a visa or may stay visa-free, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or visa-free stay ends.

The excerpts do not cover whether your child holds or can obtain Indian citizenship. The Indian embassy or consulate responsible for your area is the place to ask.

rows.question: Does our newborn need a residence permit?
rows.reply:
German law sets out when a child born in Germany is given an Aufenthaltserlaubnis (residence permit). Which of these rules applies to your child is decided by the authorities, not here.

Residence rules for a child born in Germany (AufenthG §33):
- If at the time of birth both parents, or the parent with sole custody, hold "eine Aufenthaltserlaubnis, eine Niederlassungserlaubnis oder eine Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU", the child is granted the Aufenthaltserlaubnis "von Amts wegen" (by the authority on its own initiative).
- If only one parent holds one of these, the child "kann" (may) be granted the Aufenthaltserlaubnis on the authority's own initiative.
- If the mother or father holds a visa at the time of birth, or may stay without a visa, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or lawful visa-free stay ends.

German citizenship by birth (StAG §4):
- A child becomes German at birth if one parent is a German citizen.
- A child of foreign parents born in Germany becomes German at birth if one parent (1) has lawfully had their habitual residence in Germany for five years and (2) holds an unlimited right of residence, or a residence permit as a Swiss citizen or a Swiss citizen's family member under the 1999 EU–Switzerland free movement agreement.
- When the birth is registered, the registry office asks whether a parent holds such a right. It obtains written information from the local foreigners' authority, then checks whether the child became German and records the result (PStV §34).

The excerpts do not say how or where to apply for the child's permit. Your local foreigners' authority is responsible for residence matters. The registry office that registers the birth checks citizenship.

rows.question: We are getting Mutterschaftsgeld. Does that reduce our Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under federal law, Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is credited against Elterngeld (parental allowance). BEEG §3(1) lists among the income that "auf das ... Elterngeld angerechnet" (is credited against Elterngeld) the Mutterschaftsgeld under the Fifth Book of the Social Code and the employer's supplement under MuSchG §20, in each case "für die Zeit ab dem Tag der Geburt des Kindes" (for the period from the day of the child's birth). The one-off Mutterschaftsgeld of at most 210 euros paid under MuSchG §19(2) to women who are not members of a statutory health insurer is excluded from this.

The 300-euro amount that is otherwise free from crediting does not protect against this. BEEG §3(2) says that up to 300 euros Elterngeld is free from crediting "soweit nicht Einnahmen nach Absatz 1 Satz 1 Nummer 1 bis 3 auf das Elterngeld anzurechnen sind" (unless income under numbers 1 to 3, which includes maternity benefits, is to be credited).

The federal family portal explains the effect for maternity benefits for the same child. They are credited in full ("komplett auf das Elterngeld angerechnet"). If the maternity benefits are higher than the Elterngeld, only the maternity benefits are paid. If the Elterngeld is higher, the difference is paid as Elterngeld. Months in which maternity benefits for the same child are due count as months of basic Elterngeld, even if they are due for only one day in that month.

Crediting is by the day. Under BEEG §3(1), if the income is due for only part of a month of the child's life, it is credited only against the corresponding part of the Elterngeld. The portal says the remaining days of that month are paid as a proportional share of Elterngeld.

The crediting applies to the mother's Elterngeld only. The portal states that the maternity benefits are not credited against the father's Elterngeld ("nicht auf das Elterngeld angerechnet, sondern nur auf das Elterngeld der Mutter").

Whether and how much Elterngeld your family receives is decided by the Elterngeld office for your district, not by this service.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law allows paid work while receiving Elterngeld (parental allowance), as long as it is not full-time work. One of the conditions for Elterngeld is that the person carries out "keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit" (no work, or no full-time work) (BEEG §1(1) no. 4).

The law treats a person as not working full-time if any one of these applies (BEEG §1(6)):
1. their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week, averaged over the child's month of life ("32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats");
2. they are in employment for vocational training ("Beschäftigung zur Berufsbildung");
3. they work as a suitable childminder within the meaning of §§ 23 and 43 of Book VIII of the Social Code ("geeignete Kindertagespflegeperson").

Working affects the amount. For months after the birth in which you earn less on average than before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as the relevant percentage of the difference between the two incomes. For this, income before the birth counts up to at most 2,770 euros (BEEG §2(3)).

Instead of one month of the basic payment, a parent can take two months of the Plus variant (BEEG §4(3)).

If the application states that you expect to have earnings during the payment period, the amount is first decided provisionally (BEEG §8(3) no. 3). After the payment period ends, you must prove your actual earnings for that time (BEEG §8(1)). If the application said you would have no earnings and you do, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation ("unter dem Vorbehalt des Widerrufs") (BEEG §8(2)).

The official family portal notes that these explanations cover children born after August 2021, and that partly different rules apply to children born before 1 September 2021.

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive while working, is decided only by the Elterngeld office (Elterngeldstelle) responsible for your area.

rows.question: Where and how do we apply for Kindergeld?
rows.reply:
Where to apply: the law says Kindergeld (child benefit) must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"), and the application should be made to the Familienkasse responsible under BKGG §13 (BKGG §9(1)). Under §13(1), that Familienkasse is determined in this order:
1. The Familienkasse for the district where the entitled person has their residence (Wohnsitz).
2. If they have no residence in Germany, the one for the district where they habitually stay (gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt).
3. If they have neither in Germany, the one for the district where they work.
4. In all other cases, the Familienkasse Bayern Nord.
This Familienkasse receives the application and decides on the claim (BKGG §13(1)). The Familienportal tells you to submit the application to "der Familienkasse Ihrer Agentur für Arbeit", the Familienkasse of your local employment agency.

Who applies: Kindergeld is paid to only one person per child (BKGG §3(1)). If the child lives in the parents' shared household, the parents decide between themselves who is the entitled person. If they do not decide, the family court decides on application (BKGG §3(2)). Besides the entitled person, anyone with a legitimate interest in the payment may also file the application (BKGG §9(1)).

How to apply: you can apply electronically or in writing, using the Familienkassen form. You can fill it in online, then print and sign it. For newborn children, you can apply fully online with a valid ELSTER certificate, without printing or signing by hand. In the application you must give your tax identification number (steuerliche Identifikationsnummer) and your child's. Questions about applying go to the free Bundesagentur für Arbeit service line, 0800 4 555530 (Familienportal).

Supporting documents: for a child under 18, usually only the two tax identification numbers are needed. For a child born abroad or living abroad, submit a copy of the foreign birth certificate or another official document certifying the birth. Documents can be sent online to your Familienkasse. If more documents are needed, the Familienkasse will tell you by when. Late documents can delay the application or lead to rejection (Bundesagentur für Arbeit).

Backdating: according to the Familienportal, Kindergeld can be paid retroactively for up to 6 months. To claim earlier months, state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when.

Whether you are entitled, and to how much, is decided by your responsible Familienkasse.

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Bavaria is outside the states this product covers. We cover federal law, Hessen state procedures and the Indian consular track. For how Elterngeld (parental allowance) is applied for and processed in Bavaria, contact the Elterngeld office responsible for Bavaria or the Bavarian state's official family-benefits portal.

The federal rules in the Federal Parental Allowance and Parental Leave Act (BEEG) apply everywhere in Germany, including Bavaria. On self-employment, they say the following.

Self-employed income counts. Elterngeld is 67 percent of income from work before the birth. That income includes positive income from agriculture and forestry, a trade or business ("Gewerbebetrieb") and self-employed work ("selbständiger Arbeit") that is taxable in Germany, after deductions for taxes and social contributions (BEEG §2(1)).

The percentage changes with income. It rises toward 100 percent where pre-birth income was below 1,000 euros. It falls toward 65 percent where pre-birth income was above 1,200 euros (BEEG §2(2)).

There is a floor and a ceiling. The maximum is 1,800 euros a month for full months with no income from work (BEEG §2(1)). The minimum is 300 euros, including for people with no income from work before the birth (BEEG §2(4)).

Working after the birth is allowed within limits. If you earn less after the birth than before, Elterngeld is paid on the difference. Pre-birth income is counted only up to 2,770 euros for this calculation (BEEG §2(3)). A person counts as not fully employed if their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week on average over the month of the child's life (BEEG §1(6)). Self-employed people who are temporarily not working still count as employed under the Act (BEEG §1(6a)).

An income limit applies. There is no entitlement if taxable income in the last completed tax assessment period before the birth was more than 175,000 euros. Where another person also qualifies, the limit applies to the combined income of both persons (BEEG §1(8)).

Decisions can be provisional, and income may have to be proven later. The amount is decided provisionally, based on the information you have shown to be credible, in any of these three cases (BEEG §8(3)):
1. The tax assessment for the last completed period before the birth is not yet available, and it cannot yet be said whether the 175,000-euro limit is exceeded.
2. Income from work before the birth cannot be determined.
3. The application says you expect to have income from work during the period you receive Elterngeld.

If you stated expected income in the application, you must prove your actual income for that time after the period you received Elterngeld ends (BEEG §8(1)). If you stated you expected no income, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation if you do have income after all (BEEG §8(2)).

Basic and Plus variants exist. Elterngeld is paid as Basiselterngeld or Elterngeld Plus. Basiselterngeld can be received up to the end of the child's 14th month of life. One month of Basiselterngeld can be taken as two months of Elterngeld Plus (BEEG §4(1), §4(3)).

These are the general rules only. Whether you qualify and how much you would receive is decided by the Elterngeld office responsible for your district in Bavaria.

rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
We cannot fill in your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application for you. Completing it means choosing which months to claim and entering your own income and circumstances. Those are decisions about your individual case, and only the responsible authority assesses them.

Here is what the law says the application involves.

- Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen", BEEG §7(1)).
- The application must state for which months of the child's life you claim Basiselterngeld, Elterngeld Plus or Partnerschaftsbonus (BEEG §7(1)). You can change these choices until the end of the payment period. A change applies retroactively only for the last three months before the month the change request is received (BEEG §7(2)).
- Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month the application is received. Earlier months are not paid (BEEG §7(1)).
- The person applying must sign the application. The other entitled parent must also sign it to confirm they are aware of it. The exceptions are the case in §4c and an application by a person with sole custody (BEEG §7(3)).
- If you give expected earnings in the application, you must prove your actual earnings for that time after the payment period ends (BEEG §8(1)).
- According to the federal family portal, you attach your child's birth certificate and proof of your previous income. Which income documents you need depends on whether you are employed, self-employed, a civil servant or a soldier (familienportal.de).

The responsible authority is the one your Land designates for the district where your child lives when you first apply (BEEG §12(1)). In practice, this is the Elterngeld office for your district. It decides your application.

rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
Whether your application will be approved is a decision about your family's individual case. I cannot assess it or predict the outcome. Only the responsible Elterngeld office decides. What I can give you is the conditions the law attaches.

Who is entitled. Under BEEG §1(1), a person is entitled to Elterngeld (parental allowance) if they meet all four conditions: they have a residence or habitual stay in Germany; they live in one household with their child; they look after and bring up the child themselves; and they are not working, or not working full time. Under §1(6), a person is not working full time if their working hours do not exceed 32 hours a week on average over the month of the child's life ("32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats"), if they are in vocational training, or if they work as a suitable childminder under §§23 and 43 SGB VIII.

Parents who are not EU free-movement citizens. Under §1(7), such a person is entitled only if one of these applies:
1. They hold a permanent settlement permit or an EU long-term residence permit.
2. They hold an EU Blue Card, an ICT card, a mobile ICT card, or a residence permit that allows or allowed work for at least six months. Exceptions apply to permits issued for certain purposes, including training, au pair or seasonal work, European voluntary service, job seeking, study, recognition of foreign qualifications, and certain humanitarian grounds. For some of these the exception applies only if the person is not working, not on parental leave, and not receiving SGB III benefits.
3. They hold one of the humanitarian permits named in number 2(c), and they are lawfully working, on parental leave under §15, or receiving ongoing SGB III benefits.
4. They hold one of those humanitarian permits and have stayed in Germany lawfully, with permission, or tolerated for at least 15 months.
5. They hold an employment toleration under §60d with §60a(2) sentence 3 of the Residence Act.

Income limit. Under §1(8), the entitlement lapses if the person's taxable income in the last completed assessment period before the birth was more than 175,000 euros ("mehr als 175 000 Euro"). If another person also meets the household condition, the limit applies to the sum of both persons' taxable income.

The application. Under BEEG §7(1), Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). It is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

Who decides. The Elterngeldstelle for your district decides whether these conditions are met in your case.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
How much tax you would save by changing tax class is a tax calculation for your household. This service cannot work that out or say whether switching is a good idea. That belongs to a Steuerberater (tax adviser) or your Finanzamt (tax office).

What the excerpts do say is how a tax class change before the birth is treated when parental allowance is calculated.

- Parental allowance is calculated from income in the twelve calendar months before the month of the birth: "die zwölf Kalendermonate vor dem Kalendermonat der Geburt des Kindes" (BEEG §2b(1)).
- The flat-rate income tax deduction in that calculation is based on your tax class and, where relevant, the factor under §39f of the Income Tax Act. Tax class VI is not taken into account (BEEG §2e(3)).
- If you changed tax class before the birth, the most recent tax class is used: "Für die vereinfachte Berechnung des 'Elterngeld-Nettos' kommt es auf die neueste Steuerklasse an." The older class is used only if it applied for longer within the whole assessment period than the newer one: "wenn diese innerhalb des gesamten Bemessungszeitraums länger gegolten hat als die neuere."
- A further change of tax class after the birth no longer affects parental allowance: "Ein erneuter Wechsel der Steuerklasse nach der Geburt hat also keine Auswirkung mehr auf Ihr Elterngeld."
- The Elterngeldstelle works out the net income figure used for the calculation from your gross income, using a simplified method.

What this means for your own parental allowance is decided by the Elterngeldstelle for your district. For the tax effect of switching, ask a Steuerberater or your Finanzamt.
